cells.tense: The careful work is running clean and it is not costing you anything.
cells.act: return to the work daily until it is profound
cells.ask: Take the thing you are refining and give it today's pass, the same size as yesterday's, no bigger—then close it and stop for the day.
cells.core:
The careful work is holding. You put something in front of yourself, you turn it until you can see its true edge, and you act on that instead of on what you were told to see. Not many people do that, and it is a floor you are standing on now, not an effort you are making. The hours no one watches you sort are where the depth comes from, and they are well spent.

The build gets deep by being done again, not by being watched while it is done. Give the thing you are refining today's pass, the same as yesterday's. Then close it. If you keep the practice small and repeated, it becomes the ground the rest of the day stands on, and you will feel the difference in how steady the rest of it goes.
cells.sheetLine: The work is clean and the rhythm is daily. Keep it small.
cells.verb: Sorting what matters from what doesn't by careful, repeated attention
cells.place: Where fair proportion is restored and held

cells.tense: You are sharpening the next distinction before anyone has asked for it.
cells.act: do the next piece of it in front of the person it is for
cells.ask: Do the next part of the work where the one who will use it can watch you at it, and if they say something about what it took, let that stand.
cells.core:
The distinctions you are drawing are sound and they are arriving early. You keep working one layer below where the question actually sits, so the thing is solved before the one who needs it knows there was a problem, and nothing you spent on it shows anywhere they could see.

What is thin here is not restraint. It is contact—being inside the work while someone who matters can still watch you make it. Do the next piece out in the open, in front of whoever it serves, and when they speak to what it took, do not wave it off. The work loses nothing by being seen. It gets carried instead of only held.

cells.tense: The careful work goes on, but the exchange around it has stopped.
cells.act: let the exchange with someone run both ways
cells.ask: When something comes back your way that matches what you put in—a favor, a hand, an offer—take it, say yes once, and nothing more.
cells.core:
You keep making the careful distinctions, and they are landing next to nobody who is currently picking them up. The work itself is fine; the outflow is running and the return is not, and the gap has been open long enough that it feels like the shape of things.

Do not try to push feeling into that cold spot. Let one exchange close. When something is offered that matches what you gave, take it. One yes is enough for this, and no thank-you speech is needed on either side. What changes is small and real: something you put out arrives back where you can hold it, and the careful work gets a second person present instead of a mirror.

cells.tense: You finished the thing and you are already sorting the next one.
cells.act: walk through the thing you built and touch nothing
cells.ask: Go through something you already completed—the finished version, as it stands—and change nothing while you are there, no fixing and no adding.
cells.core:
Something you made is standing complete, and the hand that made it has already moved on to the next problem. The finishing was yours, and it went by without you stopping in it, so what you arrive at keeps feeling like it simply showed up. It did not. You drew each of those lines.

The move here is smaller than it sounds. Go and look at one finished piece as it already is. Use it the way it was built to be used, or just walk through it, and change nothing while you are there. The satisfaction gets somewhere to land, and the hand that made the thing gets to know it made it.
cells.sheetLine: You finished it and kept walking. Stand in it once.
